title: instant-break and fluid blocks: start-only acceptance, water replacement, cascades (Шаг 18)
notes: Шаг 18 diagnosis + vanilla rules. Row 'hold' (z=-34) and row 'tap' (z=-30) carry the same nine blocks, built by Get-S14Commands from the platform plus each cell's own commands: land plants (short_grass, leaf_litter, dandelion) sit in the feet cell (y=201) on a dirt support so the straight-down crosshair reaches them; seagrass sits in a 1x1 one-deep walled pool (feet wet, eyes dry); tall_seagrass fills a two-deep walled pool (lower y=201, upper y=202); kelp fills a three-deep walled pool (kelp_plant, kelp_plant, kelp[age=5]); the waterlogged bottom slab and the waterlogged bottom stairs are on the platform top (y=201, hardness 2.0) so a break must leave water; the last cell is a plain walled water source that is only observed. A is teleported into the cell (x+0.5, z+0.5, pitch 90) and either holds attack for holdMs or taps it for tapMs. Every cell is one block and the rows are separate, so a hold that outlives the instant break only starts a stone dig whose packets are filtered out by position. Ours needs -HardnessReport and -OursDevGeometry (the runner writes the same command list there); vanilla builds it through the console. Traces: A gives the serverbound player_action start/finish/abort per cell and the clientbound block_changed_ack; B gives the crack stages, level_event 2001, block_update of the replacement state and any neighbour updates. The artifact s14-samples.json carries all of it for the rule tables. A kind may carry 'rows' to run only in some rows: the waterlogged slab/stairs are hold-only (a 500 ms tap cannot open a hardness 2.0 block) and the dandelion is hold-only (its first tap read hit the support below; the short-grass and leaf-litter taps already prove the start-only instant rule).
